A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Doubly Optimal Policy Evaluation for Reinforcement Learning. Their complete 28-page contents, including Appendix A proofs and Appendix B experiment details, are readable and can be matched across versions.

before.justification: Section 7 reports original Gridworld and MuJoCo experiments, including estimation errors, relative variances, and sample requirements in Figures 1–2 and Tables 1–2.

after.justification: v2 retains these original Gridworld and MuJoCo experimental results and their supporting details in Appendix B.

M1.justification: The optimal behavior policy, action-value baseline, recursive estimator, and FQE-based Algorithm 1 are unchanged. The added explanation of constructing nu in Section 6 summarizes the procedure already documented in v1 Appendix B, Equation 38.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same 1,000- and 27,000-state Gridworlds and five MuJoCo tasks: Ant, Hopper, InvertedDoublePendulum, InvertedPendulum, and Walker. No dataset, task, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Every benchmark retains on-policy Monte Carlo, ODI from Liu and Zhang (2024), and DR from Jiang and Li (2016). The newly cited papers are not added as evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Section 7 and Appendix B retain the same metrics, 1,000-episode offline datasets, training/test tuning procedure, and model settings. MuJoCo still uses horizon 100 and discretizes the first action dimension while PPO controls the remaining dimensions.

E4.justification: Neither version introduces a separate ablation, sensitivity, distribution-shift, or error-analysis experiment. The benchmark analyses and discussion of hyperparameter robustness are retained without additional tests.

E5.justification: Both report 30 independent runs for each of 30 target policies and show standard-error bands. v2 adds 900-run averaging to the Table 2 caption, but v1 Appendix B.2 already explicitly reported this for every Table 2 entry.

E6.justification: Figures 1–2 and Tables 1–2 retain the same results. DOpt's Gridworld relative variances remain 0.274 and 0.283; its MuJoCo episode counts remain 492, 372, 426, 225, and 475. Rankings and the reported 50.8%–77.5% sample savings are unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 3 replaces v1's explicit finite state-space definition with a duplicate finite action-space phrase, leaving the state-space assumption unstated. This is a limited omission in the formal setup, not evidence of a theoretical generalization. The theorem statements and Appendix A derivations otherwise remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims of joint policy/baseline optimality, unbiasedness, variance reduction that compounds over the horizon, and superior empirical sample efficiency.

C2.justification: Both retain the same explanations of variance reduction, interpretation of the differing DR/ODI rankings, and limitation concerning insufficient offline data. The recommendation to use on-policy evaluation when the learned policy and baseline are inaccurate is unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 removes Section 7's implementation-availability statement and the footnote 'Link available upon publication.' Neither PDF supplies a usable code link, so actual resource withdrawal is not established. Algorithm 1, hyperparameters, and Appendix B implementation instructions are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations concerning safety-constrained evaluation (Chen et al., 2024), multi-policy evaluation (Liu et al., 2024b), and stochastic approximation with Markovian noise (Liu et al., 2024a). Section 2's substantive comparisons and novelty positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: There are localized rewrites in the background, learning and experiment descriptions, and Appendix B, plus an expanded author name and bibliographic editing. The section sequence remains stable. Some grammatical errors are corrected, while others, including the duplicated action-space phrase, are introduced.

P2.justification: v2 adds the ICLR 2025 running header, adjusts equation spacing and pagination, and places Theorem 3's existing proof on the same page as its statement. Captions receive small edits, including source attribution for Figure 3. All plots, images, table structures, axes, and legends are retained.

improvement.justification: The method, proof derivations, experimental evidence, and conclusions are retained. Added citations, Figure 3 attribution, and clearer references to existing appendix information provide small editorial benefits, while the malformed MDP definition reduces precision. Removing the code-release placeholder changes no supplied resource. These limited benefits and defects do not establish a meaningful net change in overall quality.
